Architecture-independent scheduling container algorithms: weighted actual-runtime accounting with fractional carry, fair red-black ordering and monotonic floor including active harts and pending yield; eligibility-filtered selection; three-level MLFQ cumulative budgets and epoch boosting. These scalar/container algorithms are direct primitives; the existing Run/Dispatch/Suspend/Yield graphs retain execution and lock handoff. No allocator calls or process-lock acquisition in selection.

Internal ReadyQueue implementation/API for pure policy model; immutable mode, local queue lock and embedded metadata. Constructor/name probes are primitives; no scheduler lifecycle resources allocated. Policy entry classes may derive from this adapter; the queue storage and original algorithms are unchanged.

Single-lock bridge from stable Process descriptors to actual scheduling algorithms and platform time. Enqueue/start/stop assert process-lock ownership; take never acquires it, and tick only takes queue exclusion. Returned descriptors retain Runnable lifetime protection; no unlocked tree edits or per-dispatch allocation.
Concrete FairPolicy binds the shared PolicyReadyQueue adapter to Kind::Fair at construction. No queue algorithm, runtime loop or lock protocol is duplicated.
Concrete RoundRobinPolicy inherits original FIFO ordering and timer preemption; its name identifies the actual policy. Common execution mechanics now reside in runtime/scheduler_runtime.*.
Concrete MlfqPolicy binds the shared adapter to Kind::Feedback. Existing cumulative budgets, FIFO levels, epoch boosting and queue exclusion are reused unchanged.

excluded_execution_primitives: Register/CSR/assembly operations, compact bitset policies, stable scans, fixed table transfers and simple delegates are intentionally direct; their outer complex orchestration uses graphs.
